request.spec:
A button downloads the pools as a CSV file: a header line pool,member,share,cut then one line per
member, pools in the order added and members in the order added, a pool member as pool:<name>, the
cut as shown (empty when none).

agent.result_text:
I added an **Export pools (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-pools"`), and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` now pass.

**The export:** the new file is `src/main/frontend/features/export/exportPools.slot.tsx`, and it works the same way as the existing people and claims exports. It writes the header `pool,member,share,cut`, then one line per member, with pools and members both in the order added. A member that is another pool is written as `pool:<name>`, and the cut is written as the pool row shows it, empty when there is none. Values containing commas are quoted, e.g. `"Lee, Jo"`. No server or data changes were needed, because the pools endpoint already returns everything the file needs.

**A bug the test exposed:** retiring a person didn't refresh the pools, so the pool rows on screen kept showing the old cuts. I made two changes:
- **Retire and unretire** now also refresh the pools (`features/retire/retire.slot.tsx`), so the cuts on screen update straight away.
- **The export reloads the pools** before writing the file. Without this, any other action that changes the cuts without refreshing the pools would still produce an out-of-date file.
